description:
## Outcome

        Durable Jidoka sessions and snapshots store only portable environment bindings, checkpoints, and confirmed evidence. Recovery and session fork use the lifecycle port safely.

        ## Why now

        The lifecycle port is useful only after sessions can recover it without storing provider handles. This must exist before CLI cells or write tools use constrained execution.

        ## Current state

        `Session.Data`, snapshots, store transitions, DETS, leases, and safe session fork already exist. `Session.Execution.durable_checkpoint/6` atomically records turn snapshots, but it has no environment binding. Existing durability, crash recovery, and fork tests are strong templates.

        ## Ownership and boundary

        This is a `jidoka` change. Session data owns the portable binding state and lifecycle sequencing. Adapters own live handles. The CLI sees only public projected evidence. Do not put runtime profiles or CLI artifact paths into the session schema.

        ## Detailed implementation

        1. Version `Session.Data` and snapshot data to add optional binding, checkpoint, lifecycle status, and projected evidence.
2. Extend store transitions so a turn checkpoint and its environment checkpoint update one session revision atomically.
3. On a new sequence, resolve/open as configured, store the portable binding, and acquire only for active work.
4. On recovery, restore from the latest valid checkpoint, verify new evidence, then acquire.
5. On session fork, call environment fork only from an immutable stored checkpoint. Keep the source unchanged and reject unsupported fork.
6. Close transient handles after every turn or sequence terminal state. Apply explicit retention policy before cleanup; do not silently destroy resumable state.
7. Reject stale, cleaned, mismatched, nonportable, or weaker restored bindings.

        ## Acceptance criteria

        - [ ] In-memory and DETS stores round-trip a session binding without a live value.
- [ ] Turn and environment checkpoints commit at one session revision.
- [ ] Recovery calls restore and acquire once and validates confirmed evidence.
- [ ] Fork creates distinct child binding and checkpoint while the source remains unchanged.
- [ ] Error and cancellation close the acquired handle.
- [ ] Cleanup marks the binding terminal and later acquire/restore/fork fail.
- [ ] Existing sessions without an environment still load and run.

        ## Test plan

        - Success: DETS restart, recovery, resume, and fork with the deterministic conformance adapter.
- Invalid input: old schema, stale revision, mismatched profile digest, malformed checkpoint, and cleaned binding.
- Runtime failure: crash between intent and result checkpoint, restore failure, close failure, and cleanup failure.
- Boundary and security: inject a PID or credential into an adapter binding and assert atomic rejection.
- Deterministic capability: fake adapter, session store, lease clock, IDs, LLM, and operations.
- JSONL and exit status: public projection is JSON-safe; CLI output remains out of scope.

        ## Documentation

        Update sessions, stores, snapshots, recovery, and constrained-execution guides. Add a lifecycle table for terminal, resumable, retained, and cleaned states.

        ## Non-goals

        Do not add a CLI selector. Do not implement an adapter. Do not store open handles. Do not make cleanup implicit for a resumable checkpoint.

        ## Dependencies

        Blocking issues:

        - `jido_cli-tqg.3.4` — Implement the execution-environment lifecycle manager
- `jido_cli-tqg.2.1` — Add a public ordered Jidoka session sequence

        Features unlocked by this story:

        - One durable constrained environment per automation cell
- Safe environment cleanup after cancellation
- Checkpoint-backed coding edits

        ## Commit plan

        Create exactly one focused `jidoka` commit. Use a message such as `feat(jidoka): persist portable execution bindings (jido_cli-tqg.3.5)`. Do not include another backlog feature.

        ## Verification commands

        ```sh
        cd /Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_cli/jidoka
mix test test/jidoka/execution_environment/session_durability_test.exs test/jidoka/harness_store_durability_test.exs test/jidoka/session_test.exs
mix quality
mix test
mix docs
        ```
title: Persist portable execution bindings through recovery and fork
